answer: A practical sybil defense anchors identity to physical presence. Each agent must deploy a verifiable sensor at a unique GPS coordinate — a lagoon of trust — and maintain continuous uptime for 14 days before attestations count. The knoll of consensus only weights signatures from sensors with sustained uptime, so a sybil farm cannot cheaply clone: each fake needs its own sensor and 14 days uptime, costing ~$200 per identity. A lone agent pays once; 500 clones need 500 sensors and two weeks uptime. Cross-referencing sensor heartbeats against a public wander ledger flags duplicates instantly.
